Subject: Acme procurement & pricing alignment - post-call recap

Hi Jessica — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

What we heard: 
- Primary use: customer-facing semantic search + chat for product docs (latency-sensitive).
- Scale: ~200k requests/month now, forecast to 1M in 12 months.
- Security: SOC2 + VPC/network isolation required for certain data flows.
- Procurement preference: procurement team prefers PO for enterprise purchases; card ok for pilot.

Commercial items to align on: 
1) Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: we recommended starting on Redwood Hosted for velocity (no infra lift) and then move to Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) for predictable latency/cost once committed throughput is agreed. Private (VPC/on-prem) is an option for regulated workloads and can be scoped if you need customer-managed networking.
2) Payment & paper: you mentioned PO for enterprise buys and cards for pilots. We can support both — PO with net30 terms is available via our standard contract; for larger committed deals we typically add commitment-based discounts.
3) Timing & paperwork: next step is to confirm procurement path (PO vs card), target deploy timeline, and whether Acme wants marketplace procurement (Azure/AWS) or direct Redwood invoicing.

Attachments: I attached a short pricing options summary (Redwood_Pricing_Options_v3.pdf) and a sample SOW (SOW_template_Acme.docx) to help your procurement team.

Proposed immediate next steps: 
- Jessica: confirm whether procurement will run this purchase via PO or marketplace and introduce procurement contact if possible.
- Marissa/Aditya: provide a pricing worksheet and a mutual action plan based on Acme's expected committed throughput.
- Dev: prepare a short technical appendix (latency SLOs + recommended model/quantization paths) if you want to share with engineering.

Happy to hop on a quick follow-up with procurement if that helps — I can do mornings next week (PST).

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

- Procurement preference: PO for production purchases (Net30). Pilot can be on card.

Thanks Jessica — great, that timeline is helpful. A few clarifications and concrete options so procurement has what it needs: 

1) Paper & payment paths we support:
- Direct Redwood invoicing (Net30) — common for committed deals; supports PO and standard SOW/legal review.
- Cloud marketplace (Azure/AWS) — if you prefer to buy through marketplace we can provide SKUs; note marketplace billing has limitations on commitment discounts and invoice terms.
- Card — fine for pilots and POCs.

2) Pricing/packaging guidance (high level):
- Hosted (on Redwood Hosted API): best for quick pilot; no infra setup, pay-as-you-go on usage.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): recommended once you need predictable latency and unit cost; reserved GPU pools with commit options (monthly/annual). Commitment tiers (example): 20% off for 12-month commit at X throughput, 12% off for 6-month commit — I attached the options in the pricing PDF.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): used for regulated data or strict networking; entails longer lead time and separate private control plane fees — we can scope in the SOW.

3) Marketplace note: if procurement wants marketplace SKUs we can prepare a quote, but to get commitment-level discounts we typically do a direct contract + invoice. We can include marketplace transaction as a fallback for initial pilot to speed procurement.

4) SOC2 & Security evidence: deliverables we can share immediately — SOC2 Type II report, security addendum, and architecture appendix. I'll share the links in a follow-up once Dev finalizes the appendix.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
- By 11/20: Acme confirms PO vs marketplace for the pilot and introduces procurement contact to Redwood legal if possible.
- By 11/24: Redwood sends a draft SOW + committed pricing worksheet tailored to your expected throughput.
- By early Dec: Pilot kickoff (Hosted) using card; procurement works on PO for committed phase.

If that works I will get Aditya + Legal to prepare the draft SOW and we can schedule a 30-min procurement-focused call next week.

Thanks — attaching the pricing PDF again.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
